- If sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, reduce forecasted price momentum; model tends to overreact and overshoot downward.  
- If sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is rising, cap forecast growth to avoid over-optimism; model often exaggerates upward momentum.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from -0.5 to +0.3), adjust forecast to reflect mean reversion toward prior 10-day average, not full trend continuation.  
- If model forecast spikes >10% above recent 10-day high, apply downward correction of 5–10% to avoid over-forecasting volatility.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 5 days, assume model is lagging and adjust early forecast downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment with low volatility, model tends to underpredict downside risk — increase forecast variance or add 1–2% buffer for downside.
